reference: Harris et al., RISC-V System-on-Chip Design

font_adaptation.note: Japanese font is an adaptation; proprietary book fonts are not redistributed.

wire_widths_css_pixels.note: Aggregated interface links represent several signals, not one conductor.

diagram_basis: Pinned console RTL; main slides introduce Wally, then follow SD requests and receive data, DDR3 storage and execution, drawing commands, and output. Slide 11 identifies the added integration work. Slide 12 is the sole execution-result slide. Hidden question slide 26 retains the detailed system view.

detailed_diagram.expanded: Pipeline state and operand/forwarding selectors; PC and register-file paths; address decoding and selected responses; cache/MMU interfaces; external memory, SD and graphics connections.
detailed_diagram.grouped: ALU internals, cache/MMU internals, prediction, privilege/FPU/MDU logic, instruction expansion, load/store formatting, and most clock/reset/interrupt/control nets.
detailed_diagram.highlight: Neutral signal outlines; processor internals are not marked as explained in the main talk. AMD IP retains its separate dark-blue fill.
detailed_diagram.limits: A functional projection of the configured source, not an exhaustive RTL-equivalent netlist, cycle-accurate diagram or physical placement. Crossings without junction dots do not connect nets.
detailed_diagram.supplementary_module_scope: More detailed module drawings retained as source material; not displayed in the current twenty-seven-slide deck.

board_photograph.encoding_note: The server supplied WebP despite the PNG URL. Re-encoded as PNG without changing decoded RGBA pixels; publication removes metadata.

simplified_diagrams.scope: Functional diagrams aligned with the abstract; no instruction-encoding lesson in the main talk.
simplified_diagrams.selection: Decode selects one target; the corresponding select chooses read data.
simplified_diagrams.sd_transfer: CPU issues the SD request, copies received bytes to successive DDR3 addresses, then transfers execution to the copied program; the C fragment is conceptual.
simplified_diagrams.display: A combined drawing/display block reused from official RasterIX. The same standard display configuration is verified by experiments/dvi-recovery-20261109.

board_overview.internal_circuit_example: An AND gate corresponding to the SystemVerilog expression assign y = a & b.
board_overview.code_scope: A small combinational-logic example; it is not a complete peripheral controller.
board_overview.purpose: Explain that a described circuit can be implemented inside the FPGA chip to control physical components on the board.
board_overview.research_purpose: Slide 3 groups Wally into one block, describes its HDL/textbook, and introduces the extension purpose.

fpga_resource_question_slide.scope: Generic FPGA hierarchy from Chu (2018), not a physical Artix-7 slice or measured utilization
examples: lookup table and D-type flip-flop inside a generic logic cell
block random access memory as a separate dedicated macro cell
fpga_resource_question_slide.style: RVSOC Figures 7.11 and 23.2 adapted: medium-blue chip, pale-blue category regions, white circuit symbols, black outlines; bold circuit names and regular explanations. Classification follows Chu (2018). Japanese labels use Yu Gothic; English labels use Arial.
fpga_resource_question_slide.visible_names: Full English names with abbreviations: Look-up table (LUT), D-type flip-flop (DFF), Multiplexer (MUX), and Block random access memory (BRAM). No duplicate katakana labels; functional explanations remain in Japanese.
fpga_resource_question_slide.layout: Aligned lookup-output branching, direct and registered paths, centered English resource names, a separate clock input, and evenly spaced macro-cell rows.

fpga_utilization_question_slide.scope: Historical Before/After whole-design comparison; After is the E8 recording configuration.
fpga_utilization_question_slide.presentation: Editable table, RVSOC blue header, Yu Gothic and Arial, count-derived percentages

rvsoc_adoption_question_slide.scope: Documented textbook designations and historical draft use; not an exhaustive current adoption count. Reference-only listings excluded.
rvsoc_adoption_question_slide.presentation: Editable table with the existing RVSOC-inspired blue header, pale alternate rows, black rules and Yu Gothic/Arial typography.

restored_datapath_question_slides.geometry: Keep the PC, instruction/data memory rectangles, register file and ALU positions from the single-cycle examples.
restored_datapath_question_slides.interfaces: The memory rectangles become access interfaces; explicit AD/WD/WE/RD connect through request selection, address decode and read selection.
restored_datapath_question_slides.limits: Functional mappings; no claim of actual local IROM/DTIM, complete control wiring or cycle accuracy.

wire_rendering.shafts: Filled native polygons with exact endpoint geometry.
wire_rendering.heads: Solid outline-free triangles placed after other shapes; shafts stop at the base.
wire_rendering.crossings: Gaps in the crossing segment; actual junction radius protects connected dots.
